name: YC Atlas
description: I researched all 6,077 YC startups. I wanted to know: do these startups share anything in common? And how have trends shifted over time?

Every launched Y Combinator company, embedded by what it actually does and projected onto a single map, so neighbours build similar things. Describe your own idea and it finds the nearest ones — who they are, when YC funded them, and how many survived.

images.alt: YC Atlas map of all 6,077 Y Combinator companies, clustered by what they do
Semantic cluster trends chart showing Investing & crypto falling from 6% of 2022 batches to 2% of 2026

name: GoldCall — The AI Sales Gym
description: A gym for cold calls. You call an AI prospect that talks back and stays in character the whole way through — skeptical, too busy, stalling, pushing back on every point — and difficulty runs from easy to brutal.
When you hang up, an AI coach scores the call across five sales skills, flags the moments worth reviewing, and shows you the line you should have said instead.
Cold calling, discovery, objections, negotiation, closing, gatekeepers, and voicemail practice — no roleplay partner to schedule and no one watching you fumble.

images.alt: GoldCall App Store screenshots showing the home screen, AI leads to cold call, a scored call breakdown, and feedback with better lines to say

name: Quant Alpha
description: A self-improving quant researcher agent that autonomously finds new alphas and retires decayed ones over time.
Evaluation logic is deterministic in quantitative trading, which makes it easy to see whether the agent is actually improving over time.
Self-evolving systems are interesting to me because almost no human intervention is needed for the system to learn, execute, and reflect.
Built at the AI Engineer World's Fair Hackathon hosted by Cerebral Valley.

images.alt: Dashboard showing the living fleet of alphas and the research log of births, deaths, and rejections
Backtest view of a single alpha with equity curve, Sharpe, and drawdown

name: Whois domain name finder
description: A tool for finding premium domains. It watches domain status continuously and pings you on Telegram (and elsewhere) the moment one frees up.
It can also hunt by length — 2- and 3-letter domains are the premium ones, so it keeps searching for those and tells you when one becomes available.

name: Don't waste
